extracted.intended_audience: readers of historical U.S. statutes; legal historians; researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Transcription/reproduction of pages from 'United States Statutes at Large, Volume 1' (Acts of the Second Congress), containing enacted statutory provisions such as an extension for the census return and appropriations for 1792.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension for making return of the enumeration (District of South Carolina)
rubrics_metrics.description: That it shall be lawful for the marshal of the district of South Carolina to complete and make return of the enumeration of the inhabitants of the said district, to the President of the United States, in the form and manner prescribed by the act, Act of March 1, 1790, ch. 2, intituled 'An act providing for the enumeration of the inhabitants of the United States,' at any time on or before the first day of March next, any thing in the said act to the contrary notwithstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision extends the deadline for the marshal's return of the census enumeration for the District of South Carolina to 1 March 1792. Approved March 3, 1791.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations limit for support of government (1792)
rubrics_metrics.description: That for the service of the year one thousand seven hundred and ninety-two, and the support of the civil list of the United States, including the incidental and contingent expenses of the several departments and offices thereof, there shall be appropriated a sum of money not exceeding three hundred and twenty-nine thousand, six hundred and fifty-three dollars, and fifty-six cents; that is to say:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an overall statutory cap on appropriations for civil government support in 1792 and introduces the itemized allocations that follow. Approved Dec. 23, 1791 (Chap. III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensations — President, Vice President, Chief Justice, Associate Judges, Attorney General
rubrics_metrics.description: For the compensations granted by law to the President of the United States, the Vice President, Chief Justice, Associate Judges, and Attorney General, fifty-three thousand dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific line-item appropriation allocating $53,000 for the listed high federal officers' compensations for the 1792 service year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensations — District Judges
rubrics_metrics.description: For the like compensations to the District Judges, nineteen thousand eight hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line-item appropriation: $19,800 allocated for district judges' compensations for 1792.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensations — Members of Senate and House, officers and attendants
rubrics_metrics.description: For the like compensations to the members of the Senate and House of Representatives, and the officers and attendants of the two Houses, estimated on a session of six months continuance, and including the travelling expenses of the members, one hundred and twenty-nine thousand, seven hundred and thirty dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line-item appropriation of $129,730 covering congressional members, officers, and attendants, estimated for a six-month session and including travel expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensations — Secretary and officers of the Treasury, clerks and attendants, and loan officers
rubrics_metrics.description: For the like compensations to the Secretary and officers of the several departments of the Treasury of the United States, including clerks and attendants, and the salaries of the respective loan officers, sixty thousand three hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line-item appropriation: $60,300 for Treasury Department personnel and loan officers for 1792.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensations — Secretary of State and officers
rubrics_metrics.description: For the like compensations to the Secretary and officers of the department of State, six thousand three hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line-item appropriation: $6,300 allocated for the Department of State's secretary and officers for 1792.
